capital_categories.method: Distribution (and, in New York, transmission) net plant growth split by the forward model's bau_plan.category_shares for this utility (growth / replacement / gridmod / other; status as in the utility JSON). Storm and resilience spending is not separable in Form 1 and sits inside replacement; IT and other = general and intangible plant (Form 1) plus the "other" share.

rr_bridge.note: Revenue requirement on a Form 1 functional basis for 2021 and 2025 (return on functional rate base at the allowed after-tax WACC, depreciation, O&M, taxes other than income, income taxes; general, intangible and A&G costs allocated to the scope by plant or O&M share; jurisdictional share applied), then the approved 2026 rate-case step. Computed in engine/lookback.py with the forward model's revenue-requirement structure. Customer service and information O&M (Form 1 accounts 907-910) includes C&LM programme costs recorded by the utility, so the operating group carries public-benefits-funded programme growth as well as distribution operations.

property_tax_attribution.method: Plant-related property tax = the property tax / net plant ratio (Form 1 page 262 property and real estate taxes charged, all departments, / Form 1 page 200 net utility plant, all departments) x the scope's functional rate-base plant (scope net plant + allocated general and intangible plant, after the jurisdictional share). Property tax is assessed on plant value, so a uniform ratio attributes it to plant in proportion to net book value; assessed values, local rates and special-franchise valuation differ by plant type and locality, so this is an attribution, not a measured split. Non-plant taxes = the scope's taxes other than income (as in the detailed bridge) - plant-related property tax (payroll, gross receipts, franchise, sales and use and other taxes).

2025.unit: share of net plant a year

om_normalisation.check: Not driven by pension or retiree-benefit credits: Form 1 account 926 (employee pensions and benefits) is $18.2M in 2021 and $9.7M in 2025 (positive in both years), against administrative and general costs of $218.1M and $189.7M. Reported and normalised O&M are the same.
om_normalisation.method: Normalised O&M = reported O&M (Form 1 functional basis) - non-service pension and retiree-benefit costs in administrative and general, allocated to the scope by the same O&M share as the rest of A&G and then by the jurisdictional share. The detailed bridge keeps reported O&M; the grouped view uses normalised O&M and shows the non-service change as its own reconciling line.

2021.source: Check: Form 1 account 926 is 18.2 (2021) and 9.7 (2025) $M; not credit-driven, so no normalisation is applied

2025.source: Check: Form 1 account 926 is 18.2 (2021) and 9.7 (2025) $M; not credit-driven, so no normalisation is applied

programme_normalisation.method: Normalised O&M also excludes programme costs recovered through public-benefits charges rather than base rates: Form 1 account 908 (customer assistance expenses), where Connecticut utilities book C&LM programmes (recovered through the Conservation Adjustment Mechanism) and hardship and arrearage programmes (recovered through the Systems Benefits Charge). The amount is in the scope like the rest of customer service (jurisdictional share 1.0). The detailed bridge keeps reported O&M; the grouped view shows the change as its own line (programme_outside_base_rates), so "operating" means base-rate O&M.
programme_normalisation.check: Account 908 rises $164.5M (2021) to $255.2M (2025); EIA-861 2025 reports $135.4M of CL&P efficiency and $10.0M of demand-response costs, the rest being SBC-funded hardship and arrearage programmes.
